title: Cap. VI Arg. 12: Hague reply — segregation of believers; Davenant restates the question
pass_a_gloss: To this argument the Remonstrants reply in the Hague Colloquy, p. 53: that the segregation of believers is a segregation of singular persons; for they acknowledge that believers are singular persons, p. 51. But if we mean this, that election extends itself toward certain singular persons as singular, apart from any qualities considered in them, and namely without consideration of faith, then they utterly deny that election in this way regards singular persons. But these things are easily refuted. We acknowledge that believers are singular persons; for every action is of singulars: but that by this decree, Whosoever shall have believed shall be saved, some singular persons are segregated by God unto faith or life, others being passed by — that at last we deny.
pass_b_english: The Remonstrants answer at the Hague Colloquy (p. 53): segregation of believers is segregation of singular persons — for believers are singular persons (p. 51). If we mean election reaches certain singulars as singulars, apart from any qualities in them, and especially without regard to faith, they flatly deny election regards singulars that way. Easily answered. We grant believers are singular persons — every act is of singulars. What we deny is that by Whoever believes shall be saved God segregates some singulars unto faith or life, others passed by.
source_text: Huic argumento respondent Remonstrantes in Colloquio Hagiensi, pag. 53: Segregationem credentium esse segregationem singularium personarum; agnoscunt enim credentes esse singulares personas, pag. 51. Verum si id volumus, electionem sese extendere erga personas quasdam singulares, tanquam singulares, citra ullas qualitates in ipsis consideratas, et nominatim absque consideratione fidei, tum se pernegare electionem hoc modo singulares personas respicere. Sed haec facile refelluntur. Agnoscimus credentes esse singulares personas; nam omnis actio est singularium: sed hoc decreto, Quisquis crediderit, salvus erit, segregari a Deo singulares aliquas personas ad fidem vel vitam, aliis praeteritis, id demum pernegamus.
